failures.description: Two compounding first-draft mistakes: (1) the heading text (85 characters) exceeded the 680px scene width and was clipped mid-word - genuinely unreadable, not a nitpick. (2) 'encoder-decoder attention' (26 characters) was given a 160px box, narrower than even GEOMETRY.nodeMinWidth (176px), and overflowed both sides of the box - the incoming fan-out arrow then terminated inside that overflowing text, reading as an arrow crossing a label. Fixed by shortening the heading, widening the scene to 780px, and widening the decoder boxes to 220px.

crossCaseFindingUpdated: This is the FOURTH instance across the run (after case01's arrow-through-strip, case02's arrow-through-caption, case04's arrow-through-column-label) of the same underlying shape: authored geometry overlapping unintentionally, caught only by rendering and looking. This one has a different flavour - a box's own label overflowing an explicitly-authored width that was smaller than the label needs - but the root cause is the same as the others: nothing in validateScene or sizeOf checks whether a label fits its shape, or whether an arrow's line intersects another object's bounds. Every one of the four was fixed by an ordinary coordinate/size change, never a renderer bug. This is the clearest evidence yet that a dev-time lint (label-width-vs-box-width, arrow-line-vs-label-bbox) would be worth building - not urgent (nothing was left unreadable in a finalized case), but worth naming as the run's most concrete, recurring, cross-case finding rather than four separate minor notes.
